_comment: A scheme is the setup the loop runs under: which roles exist, which identity owns
the formal verdict, which model each role uses, which gates are mandatory, what
bounds a run, and who else has a voice. Change any of it and the numbers from
before are numbers about a different system.
The rule for cutting a new scheme is mechanical on purpose: any field below
changes, the scheme number goes up. Arguing case by case about whether a change
is 'significant' is how a comparison quietly stops being one.
Each scheme is tagged `scheme/N` on the commit where it took effect, with this
descriptor in the tag message, and every telemetry record carries {id, digest} so
a measurement window can be sliced by scheme without knowing any dates.

schemes.summary: Three GitHub Apps live; author and acceptor on Haiku; the formal verdict is read from any account.
voices: EndlessZen as drevendev, formal reviews on code
schemes.note: Retired by the budget change in #213.

schemes.summary: As scheme/1 with the per-run ceilings raised. The measured day of 2026-09-06/07 lies entirely inside this scheme.
voices: EndlessZen as drevendev, formal reviews on code
schemes.note: Measured: 125 runs, $41.15, 8 requirements landed, and 65% of spend in pull requests that could no longer be accepted. Retired for that reason.

schemes.summary: The ACCEPTOR identity alone owns the formal verdict; every other account's review is evidence.
voices: EndlessZen as drevendev, formal reviews on code (read as evidence)
schemes.note: In force from the merge of #257. Neither `in_force_from` nor `commit` is a descriptive key, so filling them in here does not change the digest and does not retroactively move the records already written under this scheme.

schemes.summary: SLOPSTER joins as an external QA voice with read access only; its findings reach the loop through the intake job.
voices: EndlessZen as drevendev, owns the specification
SLOPSTER as andy-zen-dev, read-only: comments and Issues, never a formal review
schemes.note: Activated by a repository variable rather than a merge, so `commit` records where master stood at `in_force_from`: ZENDEV_QA_LOGIN was set at 2026-09-07T22:53:33Z and the intake job cannot run without it. The QA voice began commenting earlier, at 21:48Z, so telemetry records between 21:48Z and 22:53Z say scheme/3 while a third voice was already speaking — two comments, no verdict taken on either. The earlier plan named this account AndyDev; the account is andy-zen-dev.

schemes.summary: Both roles move from Haiku 4.5 to Sonnet 5; everything else exactly as scheme/4.
voices: EndlessZen as drevendev, owns the specification
SLOPSTER as andy-zen-dev, read-only: comments and Issues, never a formal review
schemes.note: The experiment decided on 2026-09-09: does a stronger model need fewer rework rounds per requirement, so that the cost of a landed requirement grows by less than the 2x per-token price? Measured against the scheme/4 day of 2026-09-08 21:24Z to 2026-09-09 21:24Z: $27.47 per day, author mean $0.445 and max $1.30, acceptor mean $0.128 and max $0.59, 22 merges, one pull request closed by the rework bound. Forecast at equal volume about $55 per day. Ceilings unchanged on purpose: the costliest runs reached 26% and 20% of them. Effort is the CLI's default; no effort flag is passed. Activated by the two model variables (ZENDEV_AUTHOR_MODEL, ZENDEV_ACCEPTOR_MODEL) after this descriptor is active and the tag is cut, so `in_force_from` and `commit` are filled after activation, which does not change the digest. The queue at activation is the M3 tail: four PARTIAL rows under rework and one blocked, with M4's fifteen rows indexed and waiting on the M3 gate.

schemes.summary: Both roles move from Sonnet 5 to Opus 5, and the per-run ceilings scale with the 2.5x token price; everything else exactly as scheme/5.
voices: EndlessZen as drevendev, owns the specification
SLOPSTER as andy-zen-dev, read-only: comments and Issues, never a formal review
schemes.note: The same question as scheme/5, one tier up: does the strongest model need so much less rework that a landed requirement costs less than the 2.5x per-token price would say? What scheme/5 measured, in its 20 live hours (2026-09-10 17:41Z to 09-11 13:40Z, after which every AUTHOR run failed on its first turn and the loop stood still until 09-14): $97.86 per day extrapolated against $27.47 on Haiku, author mean $1.336 and max $4.31, acceptor mean $0.362 and max $1.12, 18 author pull requests merged against 12, 0.44 refusals per merged pull request against 1.0, 11 of 18 accepted on the first verdict against 3 of 12, and $4.53 per merged pull request against $2.29, exactly 2.0x. Forecast at equal volume about $245 per day. Ceilings scaled 2.5x on purpose this time: the costliest Sonnet run reached 86% of its $5.00 ceiling, and a run cut by the ceiling is money spent on nothing. Effort is the CLI's default; no effort flag is passed. Activated by the four role variables (ZENDEV_{AUTHOR,ACCEPTOR}_{MODEL,BUDGET_USD}) after this descriptor is active and the tag is cut, so `in_force_from` and `commit` are filled after activation, which does not change the digest. The queue at activation: the M3 tail (REQ-MARKET-005 and REQ-VISUALIZATION-007 PARTIAL, REQ-VISUALIZATION-006 blocked) plus ten ready bug Issues from the specification owner filed while the loop stood still, with M4's fifteen rows waiting on the M3 gate. Decided 2026-09-14 as the last model experiment for now.

schemes.summary: The AUTHOR role runs no model: the researcher (EndlessZen) writes the code under the drevendev account, and the dispatcher, reading this descriptor, never starts zendev-author.yml. The ACCEPTOR stays exactly as in scheme/6, Opus 5 with a $7.50 ceiling, so every pull request is judged by the same judge as the autonomous days it is compared with.
voices: EndlessZen as drevendev, owns the specification and, under this scheme, writes the code
SLOPSTER as andy-zen-dev, read-only: comments and Issues, never a formal review
schemes.note: The question: how fast and how well does a person driving the researcher land requirements against the same gates and the same judge, and at what token cost: nothing for the author, the ACCEPTOR's per review. The autonomous days to compare with, per merged pull request: refusals 1.0 on Haiku (scheme/4), 0.44 on Sonnet (scheme/5), 0.19 on Opus (scheme/6); accepted on the first verdict 3 of 12, 11 of 18, 22 of 27; merged per day 12, 18 (in 20 live hours), 27; cost $2.29, $4.53, $8.87; the loop's own daily cost $27.47, $97.86, $239.37. From here the pull-request ledger (pulls/ in zen-telemetry, written at close by pr-ledger.yml) carries the same measures for every author, and the ACCEPTOR's runs are recorded as before. The author's branches are not claude/**, so the forge neither updates nor deletes them; docs/zendev/ENDLESSZEN_AUTHOR.md is the contract an outside author works to. The scheme takes effect when the dispatcher first reads it, which is the merge of the pull request that activates it; in_force_from and commit are filled after the tag, which does not change the digest. Decided 2026-09-15.
